title: Inference latency amplification: root cause analysis and stabilization plan
creator: Connor Lee
description: Summary: After a capacity surge on 2026-02-22 we observed sustained 95th/99th token latency amplification for a subset of hosted models. Investigation shows an emergent interaction between speculative kernel probing, attention autotiling heuristics, and the worker scheduler under mixed-concurrency traffic. This ticket tracks the RCA, short-term mitigations and longer-term stabilizations.

root_cause: A confluence of three subsystems produced a positive feedback loop under sudden high-concurrency arrival patterns: 1) scheduler probe window expansion increased the rate of speculative kernel probes; 2) attention autotiler responded to transient sequence-length distribution shifts by re-tiling kernels which invalidated cached KV layouts; 3) probe-induced kernel switches triggered batch preemption and KV cache churn, increasing end-to-end latency and causing the scheduler to probe more aggressively. The emergent behavior manifests as latency amplification rather than a single-point regression in one component.
short_term_mitigations: Rollback probe window expansion (deployed 2026-02-22) — immediate relief for majority of traffic
Introduce a fast-path guard that prevents attention re-tiling more than once per connection in 10s window
Throttle speculative probes when worker queue depth > 70% (soft cap) to avoid batch preemption
Add anomaly alert for probe/tiling flip rate exceeding 5 flips/min per worker
long_term_actions: Implement probe damping algorithm: exponentially back off probe frequency per-worker after a kernel switch
Refactor autotiler state to allow predictions based on historical seq-length per model and avoid reactive re-tiling
Design KV-cache pinning for active sessions to reduce churn during transient kernel switches
Add deterministic integration tests (synthetic mixed-seq harness) to CI that exercise probe+tiler+scheduler interactions
Surface per-request probe decisions in trace logs and Console dashboard (route-level metric) for better observability
Create a canary strategy with staged probe-damping and autotile changes across regions and Dedicated clusters
Benchmark and publish a compatibility matrix that enumerates safe kernel-switching thresholds per model family

notes: This incident emphasizes system-level emergent behaviors — single-component fixes can mask but not resolve cross-layer feedback loops.
When designing mitigations, prefer solutions with bounded cost (e.g., damping, soft-throttles) rather than heavy-handed rollbacks which hurt utilization.
Be careful with per-model heuristics; some smaller models are sensitive to kernel-switch overhead and will need conservative thresholds.
Cross-team coordination required: Runtime, Research (benchmarks), SRE (rollouts), and Product (customer knobs)
final_decision: Adopt probe damping + autotiler state refactor as the canonical fix. Rollout via staged canary; add session-level KV pinning as a follow-up experiment.
